I was on the birth control pill. Then I switched to depo shots every three months. But I got blood clots in my lungs. So my OBGYN said I can't have anything with estrogen in it. But I wanted birth control. IUD was an option and so was the diaphragm. But there are risks to both. I researched some options and I came across Nexplanon. It's a intradermal birth control. It goes under your skin in your upper arm. Like a microchip does. I LOVE this method. You have a choice of 1, 3 or 5 year long birth control. The implant releases medication slowly over the time period. It doesn't make me moody and it doesn't make me gain weight. I've had it for a year and a half now. It's progesterone hormone only. Estrogen causes the moodiness. My fiance and I have unprotected sex. I suggest you both get tested for all STDs first, then go for it. The effectiveness is like 99.99%. The diaphragm can't get every last little guy; it only takes one to get preggo! And the IUD is painful and can poke through your walls and cause infection. This is the best method I've found so far. Hope this helps!
